Equatorial Guinea

By: Annalise Lubbe | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Equatorial Guinea: Behind bars in Africa's hellhole...48 Hours after a super yacht belonging to the vice president of Equatorial Guinea is confiscated, two engineers from South Africa are put behind b

Unique Selling Point:
Two South African engineers, Frederic Potgieter (53) from George and Peter Huxham (55) from Langebaan, were arrested at a hotel in the Equatorial Guinean capital Malabo on Bioko island on the 9th of February. They were detained in the notorious Black Beach prison - the same prison Hoekwil local Daniel Janse van Rensburg spent more than 400 days after he was illegally detained in 2013. The link in both cases is the vice president of Equatorial Guinea, Teodorin Obiang, known for his lavish lifestyle and squandering of state funds.

Summary:
Early reports on a local news station in Equatorial Guinea reported Police arrested Potgieter and Huxham after they found a black bag of cocaine on a flight from Singapore. On a national broadcast station you can hear the men saying “we are innocent” The Department of International Relations and Communications have been in touch with the families and although there have been no formal charges against them in a statement from DIRCO they were charged with “possession of drugs.”

Huxham and Potgieter, employees of SBM Offshore, a Dutch oil and gas company, work in two different departments and until their arrest have not known one another. They were thrown in Africa’s hellhole, Black Beach at first while the Dutch company’s legal team gathered evidence for the case. The two men have been moved to Oveng Asem, a maximum-security prison on the eastern side of the mainland, and worse than Black Beach in terms of isolation, says an Equatorial judge, Ondo Angue Jaun Carlos, who has since fled Equatorial Guinea. “There is there is little hope for them in Oveng Asem as it is ruled by the Defense Force. The Vice President of Equatorial Guinea, Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, known as Teodorin Obiang is Minister of Defense and National Security in Equatorial Guinea. Obiang decides on your fate, says the judge.


Further information:
Daniel Janse van Rensburg knows too well what the men must be going through and their families and have been in contact with them. In Black Beach prison he saw how women and children were abused, and the atrocities. Little food, no hygiene, the worst human rights violation. Daniel had some compensation for his life in the hellhole. He sued Obiang after he managed to clear his name with the help of the same judge, Ondo Angue gathered evidence to prove Daniel committed no crime. On Daniel’s return he wrote his life story in a book Black Beach and won his case against Obiang where the High Court in Cape Town awarded him R39 million for his loss, suffering and illegal incarceration. Two Cape Town properties were seized and on 7 February a superyacht, Blue Shadow, belonging to Obiang docked in Cape Town harbour. On 9 February the two SA citizens were arrested in Equatorial Guinea. There is no coincidence here. Obiang lashed out demanding the release of the yacht saying it belonged to the Minister of Defense. To confirm this he posted on the same day on his Twitter feed: “The ministry of defense ship leaving the port of CT to Equatorial Guinea”. There is no doubt here that Obiang is the Minister of Defense for Equatorial Guinea and therefore the yacht belongs to none other than him. Speaking to a ship captain, who wants to remain anonymous, Obiang was the person he reported and who always used the yacht.

The yacht has since left Cape Town harbour and is now sitting in Walvis Bay according to the latest news. The replacement captain who was hired walked off the boat and some other crew members. There is no telling when Blue Shadow will be back in Equatorial Guinea. The question is, what will Obiang do next? says Errol Elsdon, Daniel’s legal representative who is fighting the battle for Daniel.

Evelyn Tachau-Brown, SBM Offshore media spokesperson, has been in contact with the family making sure they are informed as best she can as the legal process in Equatorial Guinea happens at a snail pace. DIRCO has tried with intergovernmental negotiations but they say it is a criminal matter (“being charged in the possession of drugs”) and there is little the South African government can do to help.

Kathy McConnacie, Peter Huxham’s partner for the last 25 years is praying for his safe return but with every day passing and no good news, she fears for his health. She sent a parcel of his medicine and a letter via the embassy which she said could not be delivered. “He suffers from anxiety and how is he going to cope in prison? " says Kathy. Black Beach is notorious for its inhumane treatment of prisoners and even killings.

The story:
We speak to Daniel Janse van Rensburg about his ordeal in Black Beach prison and the reason for writing his life story. We briefly cover the protracted legal case, the seizing of the two properties in Cape Town and the superyacht belonging to Obiang. We interview Daniel’s legal representative, Errol Elsdon about the case who will talk about the properties, the yacht and the appeals from Obiang. Daniel has not seen a penny of the R39 million he was awarded in court.

We interview Kathy at their home in Langebaan where she will share her inner thoughts about her life partner, Peter Huxham. She is in a terrible state but knows she has to be strong for Peter. We also speak to Frederick Potgieter's daughter, Jolene, who is shocked and cannot believe what her father must be going through in prison.

The Equatorial judge, Ondo Angue Jaun Carlos, who was on the bench for 20 years in Malabo was instrumental in the eventual release of Daniel. He gathered the evidence and convinced the other judges that Daniel committed no crime. It was simply a business deal that went wrong. He will give us a zoom interview from Paris where he now lives with his family after he fled for his life from his home country. In response to the two South Afrians put behind bars without any formal charges, he said: “If the SA government does not interfere, these two gentlemen could even die”. This is a serious issue”.

Visuals: Besides our own footage for the shoot, we will tap into archive visuals consisting of news clips from various stations; archive Carte Blanche stories on Daniel done in 2016 and one on Obiang done in 2004. Diana Lucas also did a story on the election in 2004 which has visuals of the country, the president and general city and country scenes to capture the political and economic landscape.
There is a short video clip of Daniel in Black Beach which he promised we can use. The quality is poor but can be used as freeze frames to capture the scene. Obiang’s Instagram has plenty of visuals of Obiang’s lifestyle and on his Twitter feed we can see the messages he posted.

Script:


Final script: Equatorial Guinea: Black Beach hell
Date: 24 March 2023
Duration: 11 Minutes


1 V/O It’s the middle of the night on the 9th of February… two South African engineers are dragged from their hotel rooms in the West African state of Equatorial Guinea… detained on drug charges.

Kathy McConnachie: He phoned me to say to me: “Kath, I don’t think I will ever see you again,” and then the phone was taken away from him.

TVGE newsclip: UP SOUND

2 V/O A local news channel says they were in possession of bags of white powder.

Frederik Potgieter: “Never in my life”
Peter Huxham: “It's not mine. It's definitely not mine”.

3 V/O Protesting their innocence, they’re at the mercy of a country with a questionable human rights record…

Masa Kekana: When was the last time you saw your dad here in George?

Jolene Potgieter: Die agste Januarie. (The eight of January.)

4 V/O Their detention thrusts them to the centre of an international controversy: is it possible they’re being used as pawns in a cruel game of tit-for-tat? Victims of a powerful - and angry - elite…

5 V/O Peter Huxham and Frederik Potgieter worked for the Dutch oil and gas company, SBM Offshore. When they were arrested at their hotel in Equatorial Guinea’s capital, Malabo, they were preparing to return home to South Africa. Peter’s partner, Kathy McConnachie, was at home when she got news of their arrest.

Kathy McConnachie: Peter’s partner: I got a phone call on the 9th. I got another call from him to say to Kathy, something strange has happened, they are knocking on my door and they want to take me away for questioning about drugs.

Masa Kekana: Now when you heard drugs, what came to your mind?

Kathy McConnachie: Well obviously they got the wrong person. Because we don’t do drugs …that’s why I said just go along and see what they want.

Masa Kekana: So you have never heard from him again since the 9th of February?

Kathy McConnachie: 22h53 yes.

6 V/O Amazingly, Peter and Frederick had never met because they worked in different offshore divisions. Their families, now bound by a shared trauma, are trying to figure out what happened.

Masa Kekana: When was the last phone call your family got from your dad?

Jolene Potgieter: Frederik’s daughter - Hy was by die hotel, (He was at the hotel.) Hy het nag gese, lekker slaap, (He said good night…”sleep well, I will see you tomorrow.”) Ek sien jou more. (I will see you tomorrow.)

Masa Kekana: With the news about his arrest what was the first thing that came to your mind?

Jolene Potgieter: Ons het nie geweet wat gaan aan nie. (We didn’t know what was happening.) My pa is glad nie enigsens te doen met sulke goed nie, (My father is not someone who would get involved with things like that.) So ons het nie geweet hoekom nie, waarom nie, niks nie. (So we didn’t know why, nothing.)

7 V/O The men’s lawyer, appointed by SBM Offshore, says his clients “unequivocally deny the accusations”.

8 V/O Equatorial Guinea was one of Africa’s poorest countries until oil was discovered in the 1990s. Its president, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, is among the world’s longest-serving rulers - and one of its richest. He calls oil “manna from heaven”, partnering with big multinationals to extract it.

Kathy McConnachie: Peter works offshore 5 weeks on, 5 weeks off. We do lots of travelling together. We do fun things together. When he is out on the water he is very happy. And otherwise the grandchildren play a big part in our lives.

9 V/O Kathy and Peter live in Langebaan on the Cape West Coast.

Kathy McConnachie: Peter is quiet, he is very giving. He wants to just do good for everybody. That is Peter.

10 V/O Frederick Potgieter’s home is in George, in the Southern Cape.

Jolene Potgieter: Meeste van die tyd as hy by die huis is (Most of the time when he is at home,) gaan vang ons vis of ons gaan kamp of ons braai by die huis.(we catch fish, or we camp or braai.)

11 V/O In this close-knit family, Jolene and her father are inseparable.

Jolene Potgieter: Hy is die man wat ek nog altyd na opgekyk het. (He is the man I’ve always looked up to.) Hy is liefdevol, hy is n mensemens. (He is loving, a people’s person.) Hy is altyd hier vir my. Altyd daar, n vris skouer. (He is always there for me, a strong shoulder.)

12 V/O The families were told Peter and Frederick were sent to Black Beach, a prison with a sinister reputation and one that gained notoriety after the controversial arrest of another South African a decade earlier.

Daniel Janse van Rensburg: To survive one night, one day in that place is a miracle. Because you are thrown into this cage. You’ve got murderers, people with serious mental issues. The women get raped, the children get raped.

13 V/O Daniel Janse van Rensburg, had been dumped into Black Beach after a deal with one of the president’s relatives, a prominent local businessman, turned sour.

14 V/O But, his actual jailer appears to have been a far more influential figure: the vice president and the man in overall charge of the country’s security and prisons. Oh, and he also happens to be the president’s son. His name is Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, known simply as Teodorin.

Daniel Janse van Rensburg: Former Black Beach prisoner: They think they are above the law the family, there is no democracy as such. And once the law doesn’t suit them then they just step above the law.

15 V/O Daniel believes he’d never have been freed had it not been for a now former judge - former, because he fled Equatorial Guinea after speaking out against corruption in the judicial system. At the time, Juan Carlos Ondo Angue was president of the Supreme Court and he found Daniel was being held without evidence.

Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: Former Chief Justice - Daniel’s case should have been brought to justice as an alleged bridge of contract, not as a criminal offense. There was no need to violate his rights as a citizen to be in prison.

Masa Kekana: So is it fair to say Daniel was actually innocent?

Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: Of course he was innocent. It was a business matter. This is not a criminal issue. Nobody should be kept in prison for that.

16 V/O After more than 400 days in appalling conditions, Daniel was freed and allowed to return home. He’s recorded his experiences in a book.

Daniel Janse van Rensburg: It was really very difficult because you have to remember all the bad things and you have to concentrate on the very things you try to forget.

17 V/O But could these two strikingly similar, but apparently unconnected incidents be linked? Is it possible Peter and Frederick are paying a grotesque price for Daniel’s pursuit of justice?

Errol Elsdon: Daniel’s advisor - When Daniel was released in 2015 from Equatorial Guinea he set about suing the vice president Teodorin Obiang on the basis that he had been the minister in charge of prisons and security at the time.

18 V/O Errol Elsdon has fought similar cases across Africa and became an advisor in Daniel’s case for damages against Teodorin. It took five years, but in a landmark ruing by the Western Cape High Court, Daniel was awarded 39-million Rand for illegal incarceration in Black Beach and torture.

To settle the court order, two Cape Town properties belonging to Teodorin, including an opulent mansion, were attached in 2021. Daniel, though, has yet to see a cent of the damages awarded.

Masa Kekana: What was causing all the delays?

Errol Elsdon: The vice president appealed every step of the way.

18 V/O But then came an incident that appears to have sealed Peter and Frederick’s fate. On the the 7th of February this year, a super-yacht called Blue Shadow believed to be another of Teodorin’s many assets, was attached in Cape Town. The move outraged the playboy vice president, who appeared to threaten reprisals in this Tweet.

VIZ: (teddy nguema @teonguema) “Return the ship to us or carry the consequences” Tweet 19 February

Masa Kekana: What do you make of the Tweet following the arrest of Blue Shadow?

Errol Elsdon: It's hardly coincidental. Clearly there is a link.

19 V/O Teodorin has been accused of corruption in various countries and is famous for his lavish lifestyle. Handed a five-year suspended jail sentence in France, he’s the target of anti-corruption sanctions imposed by the UK and has had a fleet of luxury cars seized by Swiss prosecutors.

Antony Goldman: The amount of money that came in and the speed with which money came into eg from oil so quickly in the 90 '90s into such a small country with such a distinct political culture that has created an environment in which corruption flourish and in which inequality has also increased dramatically.

20 V/O Having spent years covering stories in West Africa, journalist Antony Goldman knows Equatorial Guinea like the back of his hand.

Antony Goldman: Political Analyst - When the vice president was in South Africa and was challenged as to how he was able to finance this lifestyle on a modest official salary he was able to argue it wasn’t illegal in Equatorial Guinea to accept commissions from contractors looking for government contracts.

LINK: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in the world where the president encourages the ministers and his family members to benefit from the country’s resources, but in this case, the resource being oil, it will run out.

21 V/O Hoping it may lead to Peter and Frederik’s freedom, Blue Shadow was released after two weeks. Instead, the two men were sent to a high-security prison in Mongomo on the mainland.

Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: This prison houses mainly political prisoners and the most dangerous criminals for whom the government considers the right of visitors and medical assistance must be prohibited.

Masa Kekana: Who will ultimately decide the fate of these men?

Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: The final decision rests with the same authorities that ordered their detention, which means the highest political authority.

22 V/O Back home, the clock is ticking. The families have been in touch with SBM Offshore… and the South African government has offered support… but there’s been very little news.

Masa Kekana: If you could get a message to your father what would you say to him?

Jolene Potgieter: Ja ek wil net vir hom se, staan sterk en ons is baie lief vir hom.(I want to say, “be strong, we love you very much”.) en dat hy nie alleen is nie. (That he’s not alone.) Hy moet aanhou bid, aanhou, net vasbyt. (He must keep on praying. Hang in there.)

23 V/O On the 15th of March, company representatives managed to visit Peter and Frederik in prison - which they felt was a milestone…but the prospect of real justice is uncertain.
_________________________________________________________________________

Promos:

21 second promo:
V/O Plucked from their hotel room in Equatorial Guinea …in the middle of the night… for allegedly smuggling drugs...why were two South African engineers thrown into the notorious Black Beach prison?.

Frederik Potgieter: “Never in my life”
Peter Huxham: “It's not mine. It's definitely not mine”.

Jolene Potgieter: Ja ek wil net vir hom se, staan sterk en ons is baie lief vir hom.

21 second promo:
V/O Black Beach prison, notorious for human rights abuse and torture - the worst in Equatorial Guinea. Why were two South African engineers sent here without being formally charged?
Jolene Potgieter; 23;23 En toe sien ek van die nuus my pa en Peter op hulle nuus kanaal is en dat daar sakke vol wit poier voor hulle staan. Hulle deny alles, dit is die laaste keer wat ek my pa se gesig gesien het.

11 second promo
V/O Plucked from their hotel room in Equatorial Guinea…in the middle of the night an thrown into prison for alleged drug smuggling, we examine the fate of two South African engineers.

Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 09 April 2023 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: Final script: Equatorial Guinea: Black Beach hell Date: 24 March 2023 Duration: 11 Minutes 1 V/O It’s the middle of the night on the 9th of February… two South African engineers are dragged from their hotel rooms in the West African state of Equatorial Guinea… detained on drug charges. Kathy McConnachie: He phoned me to say to me: “Kath, I don’t think I will ever see you again,” and then the phone was taken away from him. TVGE newsclip: UP SOUND 2 V/O A local news channel says they were in possession of bags of white powder. Frederik Potgieter: “Never in my life” Peter Huxham: “It's not mine. It's definitely not mine”. 3 V/O Protesting their innocence, they’re at the mercy of a country with a questionable human rights record… Masa Kekana: When was the last time you saw your dad here in George? Jolene Potgieter: Die agste Januarie. (The eight of January.) 4 V/O Their detention thrusts them to the centre of an international controversy: is it possible they’re being used as pawns in a cruel game of tit-for-tat? Victims of a powerful - and angry - elite… 5 V/O Peter Huxham and Frederik Potgieter worked for the Dutch oil and gas company, SBM Offshore. When they were arrested at their hotel in Equatorial Guinea’s capital, Malabo, they were preparing to return home to South Africa. Peter’s partner, Kathy McConnachie, was at home when she got news of their arrest. Kathy McConnachie: Peter’s partner: I got a phone call on the 9th. I got another call from him to say to Kathy, something strange has happened, they are knocking on my door and they want to take me away for questioning about drugs. Masa Kekana: Now when you heard drugs, what came to your mind? Kathy McConnachie: Well obviously they got the wrong person. Because we don’t do drugs …that’s why I said just go along and see what they want. Masa Kekana: So you have never heard from him again since the 9th of February? Kathy McConnachie: 22h53 yes. 6 V/O Amazingly, Peter and Frederick had never met because they worked in different offshore divisions. Their families, now bound by a shared trauma, are trying to figure out what happened. Masa Kekana: When was the last phone call your family got from your dad? Jolene Potgieter: Frederik’s daughter - Hy was by die hotel, (He was at the hotel.) Hy het nag gese, lekker slaap, (He said good night…”sleep well, I will see you tomorrow.”) Ek sien jou more. (I will see you tomorrow.) Masa Kekana: With the news about his arrest what was the first thing that came to your mind? Jolene Potgieter: Ons het nie geweet wat gaan aan nie. (We didn’t know what was happening.) My pa is glad nie enigsens te doen met sulke goed nie, (My father is not someone who would get involved with things like that.) So ons het nie geweet hoekom nie, waarom nie, niks nie. (So we didn’t know why, nothing.) 7 V/O The men’s lawyer, appointed by SBM Offshore, says his clients “unequivocally deny the accusations”. 8 V/O Equatorial Guinea was one of Africa’s poorest countries until oil was discovered in the 1990s. Its president, Teodoro Obiang Nguema Mbasogo, is among the world’s longest-serving rulers - and one of its richest. He calls oil “manna from heaven”, partnering with big multinationals to extract it. Kathy McConnachie: Peter works offshore 5 weeks on, 5 weeks off. We do lots of travelling together. We do fun things together. When he is out on the water he is very happy. And otherwise the grandchildren play a big part in our lives. 9 V/O Kathy and Peter live in Langebaan on the Cape West Coast. Kathy McConnachie: Peter is quiet, he is very giving. He wants to just do good for everybody. That is Peter. 10 V/O Frederick Potgieter’s home is in George, in the Southern Cape. Jolene Potgieter: Meeste van die tyd as hy by die huis is (Most of the time when he is at home,) gaan vang ons vis of ons gaan kamp of ons braai by die huis.(we catch fish, or we camp or braai.) 11 V/O In this close-knit family, Jolene and her father are inseparable. Jolene Potgieter: Hy is die man wat ek nog altyd na opgekyk het. (He is the man I’ve always looked up to.) Hy is liefdevol, hy is n mensemens. (He is loving, a people’s person.) Hy is altyd hier vir my. Altyd daar, n vris skouer. (He is always there for me, a strong shoulder.) 12 V/O The families were told Peter and Frederick were sent to Black Beach, a prison with a sinister reputation and one that gained notoriety after the controversial arrest of another South African a decade earlier. Daniel Janse van Rensburg: To survive one night, one day in that place is a miracle. Because you are thrown into this cage. You’ve got murderers, people with serious mental issues. The women get raped, the children get raped. 13 V/O Daniel Janse van Rensburg, had been dumped into Black Beach after a deal with one of the president’s relatives, a prominent local businessman, turned sour. 14 V/O But, his actual jailer appears to have been a far more influential figure: the vice president and the man in overall charge of the country’s security and prisons. Oh, and he also happens to be the president’s son. His name is Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, known simply as Teodorin. Daniel Janse van Rensburg: Former Black Beach prisoner: They think they are above the law the family, there is no democracy as such. And once the law doesn’t suit them then they just step above the law. 15 V/O Daniel believes he’d never have been freed had it not been for a now former judge - former, because he fled Equatorial Guinea after speaking out against corruption in the judicial system. At the time, Juan Carlos Ondo Angue was president of the Supreme Court and he found Daniel was being held without evidence. Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: Former Chief Justice - Daniel’s case should have been brought to justice as an alleged bridge of contract, not as a criminal offense. There was no need to violate his rights as a citizen to be in prison. Masa Kekana: So is it fair to say Daniel was actually innocent? Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: Of course he was innocent. It was a business matter. This is not a criminal issue. Nobody should be kept in prison for that. 16 V/O After more than 400 days in appalling conditions, Daniel was freed and allowed to return home. He’s recorded his experiences in a book. Daniel Janse van Rensburg: It was really very difficult because you have to remember all the bad things and you have to concentrate on the very things you try to forget. 17 V/O But could these two strikingly similar, but apparently unconnected incidents be linked? Is it possible Peter and Frederick are paying a grotesque price for Daniel’s pursuit of justice? Errol Elsdon: Daniel’s advisor - When Daniel was released in 2015 from Equatorial Guinea he set about suing the vice president Teodorin Obiang on the basis that he had been the minister in charge of prisons and security at the time. 18 V/O Errol Elsdon has fought similar cases across Africa and became an advisor in Daniel’s case for damages against Teodorin. It took five years, but in a landmark ruing by the Western Cape High Court, Daniel was awarded 39-million Rand for illegal incarceration in Black Beach and torture. To settle the court order, two Cape Town properties belonging to Teodorin, including an opulent mansion, were attached in 2021. Daniel, though, has yet to see a cent of the damages awarded. Masa Kekana: What was causing all the delays? Errol Elsdon: The vice president appealed every step of the way. 18 V/O But then came an incident that appears to have sealed Peter and Frederick’s fate. On the the 7th of February this year, a super-yacht called Blue Shadow believed to be another of Teodorin’s many assets, was attached in Cape Town. The move outraged the playboy vice president, who appeared to threaten reprisals in this Tweet. VIZ: (teddy nguema @teonguema) “Return the ship to us or carry the consequences” Tweet 19 February Masa Kekana: What do you make of the Tweet following the arrest of Blue Shadow? Errol Elsdon: It's hardly coincidental. Clearly there is a link. 19 V/O Teodorin has been accused of corruption in various countries and is famous for his lavish lifestyle. Handed a five-year suspended jail sentence in France, he’s the target of anti-corruption sanctions imposed by the UK and has had a fleet of luxury cars seized by Swiss prosecutors. Antony Goldman: The amount of money that came in and the speed with which money came into eg from oil so quickly in the 90 '90s into such a small country with such a distinct political culture that has created an environment in which corruption flourish and in which inequality has also increased dramatically. 20 V/O Having spent years covering stories in West Africa, journalist Antony Goldman knows Equatorial Guinea like the back of his hand. Antony Goldman: Political Analyst - When the vice president was in South Africa and was challenged as to how he was able to finance this lifestyle on a modest official salary he was able to argue it wasn’t illegal in Equatorial Guinea to accept commissions from contractors looking for government contracts. LINK: Equatorial Guinea is the only country in the world where the president encourages the ministers and his family members to benefit from the country’s resources, but in this case, the resource being oil, it will run out. 21 V/O Hoping it may lead to Peter and Frederik’s freedom, Blue Shadow was released after two weeks. Instead, the two men were sent to a high-security prison in Mongomo on the mainland. Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: This prison houses mainly political prisoners and the most dangerous criminals for whom the government considers the right of visitors and medical assistance must be prohibited. Masa Kekana: Who will ultimately decide the fate of these men? Juan Carlos Ondo Angue: The final decision rests with the same authorities that ordered their detention, which means the highest political authority. 22 V/O Back home, the clock is ticking. The families have been in touch with SBM Offshore… and the South African government has offered support… but there’s been very little news. Masa Kekana: If you could get a message to your father what would you say to him? Jolene Potgieter: Ja ek wil net vir hom se, staan sterk en ons is baie lief vir hom.(I want to say, “be strong, we love you very much”.) en dat hy nie alleen is nie. (That he’s not alone.) Hy moet aanhou bid, aanhou, net vasbyt. (He must keep on praying. Hang in there.) 23 V/O On the 15th of March, company representatives managed to visit Peter and Frederik in prison - which they felt was a milestone…but the prospect of real justice is uncertain. _________________________________________________________________________ Promos: 21 second promo: V/O Plucked from their hotel room in Equatorial Guinea …in the middle of the night… for allegedly smuggling drugs...why were two South African engineers thrown into the notorious Black Beach prison?. Frederik Potgieter: “Never in my life” Peter Huxham: “It's not mine. It's definitely not mine”. Jolene Potgieter: Ja ek wil net vir hom se, staan sterk en ons is baie lief vir hom. 21 second promo: V/O Black Beach prison, notorious for human rights abuse and torture - the worst in Equatorial Guinea. Why were two South African engineers sent here without being formally charged? Jolene Potgieter; 23;23 En toe sien ek van die nuus my pa en Peter op hulle nuus kanaal is en dat daar sakke vol wit poier voor hulle staan. Hulle deny alles, dit is die laaste keer wat ek my pa se gesig gesien het. 11 second promo V/O Plucked from their hotel room in Equatorial Guinea…in the middle of the night an thrown into prison for alleged drug smuggling, we examine the fate of two South African engineers. ___________________________________________________________________________________________________

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Equatorial Guinea: Behind bars in Africa's hellhole...48 Hours after a super yacht belonging to the vice president of Equatorial Guinea is confiscated, two engineers from South Africa are put behind b
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Two South African engineers, Frederic Potgieter (53) from George and Peter Huxham (55) from Langebaan, were arrested at a hotel in the Equatorial Guinean capital Malabo on Bioko island on the 9th of February. They were detained in the notorious Black Beach prison - the same prison Hoekwil local Daniel Janse van Rensburg spent more than 400 days after he was illegally detained in 2013. The link in both cases is the vice president of Equatorial Guinea, Teodorin Obiang, known for his lavish lifestyle and squandering of state funds.
metadata.Summary: Early reports on a local news station in Equatorial Guinea reported Police arrested Potgieter and Huxham after they found a black bag of cocaine on a flight from Singapore. On a national broadcast station you can hear the men saying “we are innocent” The Department of International Relations and Communications have been in touch with the families and although there have been no formal charges against them in a statement from DIRCO they were charged with “possession of drugs.” Huxham and Potgieter, employees of SBM Offshore, a Dutch oil and gas company, work in two different departments and until their arrest have not known one another. They were thrown in Africa’s hellhole, Black Beach at first while the Dutch company’s legal team gathered evidence for the case. The two men have been moved to Oveng Asem, a maximum-security prison on the eastern side of the mainland, and worse than Black Beach in terms of isolation, says an Equatorial judge, Ondo Angue Jaun Carlos, who has since fled Equatorial Guinea. “There is there is little hope for them in Oveng Asem as it is ruled by the Defense Force. The Vice President of Equatorial Guinea, Teodoro Nguema Obiang Mangue, known as Teodorin Obiang is Minister of Defense and National Security in Equatorial Guinea. Obiang decides on your fate, says the judge.
metadata.Further information: Daniel Janse van Rensburg knows too well what the men must be going through and their families and have been in contact with them. In Black Beach prison he saw how women and children were abused, and the atrocities. Little food, no hygiene, the worst human rights violation. Daniel had some compensation for his life in the hellhole. He sued Obiang after he managed to clear his name with the help of the same judge, Ondo Angue gathered evidence to prove Daniel committed no crime. On Daniel’s return he wrote his life story in a book Black Beach and won his case against Obiang where the High Court in Cape Town awarded him R39 million for his loss, suffering and illegal incarceration. Two Cape Town properties were seized and on 7 February a superyacht, Blue Shadow, belonging to Obiang docked in Cape Town harbour. On 9 February the two SA citizens were arrested in Equatorial Guinea. There is no coincidence here. Obiang lashed out demanding the release of the yacht saying it belonged to the Minister of Defense. To confirm this he posted on the same day on his Twitter feed: “The ministry of defense ship leaving the port of CT to Equatorial Guinea”. There is no doubt here that Obiang is the Minister of Defense for Equatorial Guinea and therefore the yacht belongs to none other than him. Speaking to a ship captain, who wants to remain anonymous, Obiang was the person he reported and who always used the yacht. The yacht has since left Cape Town harbour and is now sitting in Walvis Bay according to the latest news. The replacement captain who was hired walked off the boat and some other crew members. There is no telling when Blue Shadow will be back in Equatorial Guinea. The question is, what will Obiang do next? says Errol Elsdon, Daniel’s legal representative who is fighting the battle for Daniel. Evelyn Tachau-Brown, SBM Offshore media spokesperson, has been in contact with the family making sure they are informed as best she can as the legal process in Equatorial Guinea happens at a snail pace. DIRCO has tried with intergovernmental negotiations but they say it is a criminal matter (“being charged in the possession of drugs”) and there is little the South African government can do to help. Kathy McConnacie, Peter Huxham’s partner for the last 25 years is praying for his safe return but with every day passing and no good news, she fears for his health. She sent a parcel of his medicine and a letter via the embassy which she said could not be delivered. “He suffers from anxiety and how is he going to cope in prison? " says Kathy. Black Beach is notorious for its inhumane treatment of prisoners and even killings. The story: We speak to Daniel Janse van Rensburg about his ordeal in Black Beach prison and the reason for writing his life story. We briefly cover the protracted legal case, the seizing of the two properties in Cape Town and the superyacht belonging to Obiang. We interview Daniel’s legal representative, Errol Elsdon about the case who will talk about the properties, the yacht and the appeals from Obiang. Daniel has not seen a penny of the R39 million he was awarded in court. We interview Kathy at their home in Langebaan where she will share her inner thoughts about her life partner, Peter Huxham. She is in a terrible state but knows she has to be strong for Peter. We also speak to Frederick Potgieter's daughter, Jolene, who is shocked and cannot believe what her father must be going through in prison. The Equatorial judge, Ondo Angue Jaun Carlos, who was on the bench for 20 years in Malabo was instrumental in the eventual release of Daniel. He gathered the evidence and convinced the other judges that Daniel committed no crime. It was simply a business deal that went wrong. He will give us a zoom interview from Paris where he now lives with his family after he fled for his life from his home country. In response to the two South Afrians put behind bars without any formal charges, he said: “If the SA government does not interfere, these two gentlemen could even die”. This is a serious issue”. Visuals: Besides our own footage for the shoot, we will tap into archive visuals consisting of news clips from various stations; archive Carte Blanche stories on Daniel done in 2016 and one on Obiang done in 2004. Diana Lucas also did a story on the election in 2004 which has visuals of the country, the president and general city and country scenes to capture the political and economic landscape. There is a short video clip of Daniel in Black Beach which he promised we can use. The quality is poor but can be used as freeze frames to capture the scene. Obiang’s Instagram has plenty of visuals of Obiang’s lifestyle and on his Twitter feed we can see the messages he posted. ________________________________________________________________________________________________
